No capital is named for Batbayan's last years 665-668. Reviewer ia-01-d: point moved from the gazetteer's Tmutarakan placeholder (36.72, 45.22) to the page's coordinates.

keyframe_review.note: 633-655, 0.24 M km2 (987 cells): the steppe from the Don to the Dnieper, the Azov coast, the Kuban and the Crimea. Page: Kubrat united the Onogur Bulgars with the Kutrigurs and Utigurs 'between 630 and 635'; the state was 'originally centered between the Dniester and lower Volga' with the capital Phanagoria on the Taman Peninsula. The page gives no area and no frontier; the shape stands (it lacks the Dniester side the page names, which the 656 shape adds). Years 633 against the page's 630-635 are within its range.

correction.text: the shape as drawn, for 656-667 only: the state ends in 668, so 668-673 are not this state's

keyframe_review.note: 656-673, 0.30 M km2 (1,205 cells): the 633 shape plus 226 cells west of the Dnieper (Ukraine and Moldova), all of which lie in the Avar Khaganate's 655 shape. Page: in the mid-7th century the state 'expanded west to include Avar territory' and was 'centered on Poltava'. The page ends the state in 668 ('disintegrated under Khazar attack'), five years before Cliopatria's shape does; the Khazaria dossier takes 983 of these cells in 668.

correction.text: years only: the 63,000 km2 shape between the Dniester and the Danube delta (248 cells) is Asparukh's horde, the seed of the First Bulgarian Empire, not Old Great Bulgaria: the state ended in 668

keyframe_review.note: 674-681, 0.06 M km2: Dniester steppe, Moldova and the Danube delta. Asparukh page: 'the state disintegrated under Khazar attack in 668'; Asparukh 'and his people settled in the Danube Delta' during the Arab siege of Constantinople (674-678), won at Ongal in 680 and was recognised by Byzantium in 681. The first-bulgarian-empire dossier (Cliopatria starts it in 682) should carry this 674-681 shape as its prelude.

region.text: the Pontic steppe from the Don to the Dnieper, the Azov coast, the Kuban and the Crimea, with Phanagoria on the Taman Peninsula

ledger.note: 633: Kubrat's Great Bulgaria rises on the Pontic steppe. 'Between 630 and 635' he united the Onogur Bulgars with the Kutrigurs and Utigurs and 'quickly managed to overthrow Avar domination'; infobox: Kubrat reigned 632-665, capital Phanagoria 632-665. The Tong Yabghu page has client tribes such as the Khazars and Great Bulgaria independent after the Western Turks' collapse c. 630, so the steppe came from their overlordship (western-gokturks dossier: vassal 627-630).

region.text: the steppe west of the Dnieper towards the Dniester, Avar territory

ledger.note: 656: Great Bulgaria expands west into Avar land. In the mid-7th century the state 'expanded west to include Avar territory' and was 'centered on Poltava' (page, no year); the year and the 226 cells are Cliopatria's 656 shape, which lies wholly inside the Avar Khaganate's 655 shape. Reviewer ia-01-d: confidence 1, the page says 'in the mid-7th century'; 656 is Cliopatria's year.

region.text: Asparukh's horde between the Dniester and the Danube delta

ledger.note: 668: the sons part. 'The state disintegrated under Khazar attack in 668'; Asparukh, with 30,000 to 50,000 Bulgars, goes west and 'settled in the Danube Delta' during the siege of Constantinople (674-678); Kotrag fled north up the Volga, Kuber went to Sirmium and Macedonia, Alcek to Italy c. 662 (Old Great Bulgaria page). The year of the departure is the page's; the Dniester-Danube land is Cliopatria's 674 shape.

region.text: the Pontic steppe between the Don and the Dnieper, the Kuban and the Crimea

ledger.note: 668: the Khazars take the steppe. 'The state disintegrated under Khazar attack in 668'; the Khazars page puts the subjugation of the Onoghur-Bulghar union 'sometime around 670', and the Old Great Bulgaria page says the Khazars later subjugated Batbayan, Kubrat's eldest son and successor (665-668). Matches the Khazaria dossier's 668 gain.

668: Old Great Bulgaria ends. Infobox: 'Ended: 668, when it disintegrated under Khazar attack'; rulers Kubrat 632-665 and Batbayan 665-668. Its steppe goes to the Khazars, Asparukh's horde to the Danube, Batbayan and Kotrag's people to the Volga (Volga Bulgaria).

notes:
Cliopatria row Old Great Bulgaria 633..681 (3 shapes). The page puts the end in 668 (infobox, Asparukh page), so the 674-681 shape (the Dniester-Danube horde of Asparukh) is marked wrong for this state and belongs to the first-bulgarian-empire dossier as a 674-681 prelude keyframe (the group eu-18 should add it; Cliopatria starts that state in 682). Between 668 and 674 no page places Asparukh's people, and the 669-673 years carry no Bulgar shape; the Khazaria dossier draws the steppe from 668.

Start: the page dates the unification 'between 630 and 635' and the capital from 632; Cliopatria's 633 is kept. The Pontic steppe before 633 was a Western Turk client land (western-gokturks dossier, vassal 627-630) and partly Avar; the 630-632 years are not drawn for any state.

Page budget 1-2 pages: Old Great Bulgaria and Asparukh opened; the Khazars, Tong Yabghu and Volga Bulgaria pages were opened for the Khazaria and Western Goktürks dossiers and are cited in notes only. Area: the page gives none; shapes are 0.24, 0.30 and 0.06 M km2. Not drawn: Kuber's Pannonia and Macedonia (off the steppe), Alcek's grant near Benevento c. 662, the Heraclius alliance and patrician title (page: no date). Counterparts needing dossiers: none new (first-bulgarian-empire, volga-bulgaria, khazaria, avar-khaganate, western-gokturks exist or are written).
